subject: Pilot plan: SLO constraints, concurrency & cost levers (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@pioneerretail.com>, Eric Monroe <eric.monroe@pioneerretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot plan: SLO constraints, concurrency & cost levers (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the time today — good alignment overall. Below is a concise post-call recap and a proposed pilot configuration to validate the latency/throughput targets you asked about. Attaching the SLO matrix and a short example trace.

Quick summary of your asks (from call):
- Target: 120ms p95 for single-turn generation (90–200 tokens typical).
- Streaming: yes — partial tokens must appear within 40ms of generation start for interactive UI.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state 350–450 concurrent sessions; burst to ~800 for flash sales.
- Throughput: ~15k tokens/s sustained across the fleet during peak.
- Data: customer messages only, no sensitive PII; retention policy: 30 days.

Cost/perf levers we proposed (high level):
- Continuous batching with 20–50ms batch windows (trade-off: slightly higher p50, big drop in per-token cost).
- Prefix KV caching for common system prompts & recent context (sizable win for retail chat UX).
- Quantization profile: int8 for baseline model, int4 if accuracy checks pass on eval set.
- Model variants: default to rw-instruct-large-int8; fallback to rw-instruct-small-int8 for low-latency short prompts.
- Dedicated GPU pool for the pilot (predictable tail latency) vs hosted shared with routing guardrails.

Proposed pilot (2 weeks):
1) Week 0: deploy dedicated pool (2 x 80GB A100 equiv), enable continuous batching (25ms window), enable KV cache for top-200 system prompts.
2) Week 1: ramp to 50% traffic — measure p50/p95 latency, streaming token time, and errors. Run eval prompts to verify quality delta for int8 quantization.
3) Week 2: ramp to 100% for a short stress window (simulate flash sale). Capture end-to-end traces and cost metrics.

Deliverables from our side: SLO matrix (attached), latency traces, recommended config and estimated monthly cost for sustained steady-state and burst.

Next ask from you: confirm whether Pioneer wants Dedicated pilot (recommended) or prefers Hosted with higher-cost routing. Also confirm a preferred pilot start date (we suggested Oct 25).

Attachments: pilot_slo_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_latency_trace.json (trace snippet), quant-profile-int8.csv (reference).

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga — great write-up. A couple of clarifications before we lock dates: 
1) The 120ms p95 — is that measured from our frontend send (end-to-end) or token-emit on the model side? We need end-to-end for UX reasons.
2) For concurrency: 350–450 steady is across geos (US + EU) — we'll probably run two simultaneous pilots (US primary, EU lower QPS).
3) Can you provide a back-of-envelope monthly cost for the dedicated config you suggested (the 2 x 80GB A100 equiv)? We want to compare that to hosted expected spend.

If we can get the cost estimate + a short note on how the streaming 40ms partial token constraint is measured (and observed during pilot), we're good to confirm Oct 25.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:22:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot cost + streaming validation approach

Quick stabs based on the pilot config (2 x 80GB equiv dedicated; continuous batching 25ms):

Latency assumptions (end-to-end):
- Network (customer frontend -> edge): ~10–25ms US, ~30–50ms EU (depends on CDN & WAF).
- Redwood ingress + routing + scheduling: ~8–15ms with dedicated pool and hot routing.
- Model token emit time (rw-instruct-large-int8): ~15–40ms for first token depending on prompt size.
- Typical combined p50 ~60–80ms; p95 ~110–140ms (so 120ms p95 is achievable in US with the dedicated config if we keep batch window small and KV cache hit rates high).

Streaming partial-token validation:
- We'll instrument three metrics: time-to-first-byte at the frontend, time-to-first-token at the runtime (rt.token_emit_first_ms), and client-apparent first-byte time.
- For the pilot, add a synthetic probe from Pioneer CDN -> Redwood edge that asserts first token arrives within 40ms of model-side first-token. If we see delta >40ms, we look at batching window or network tail.

Quantization recommendation: 
- Start pilot with int8 profile (quant-profile-int8.csv attached) for minimal quality risk. If eval on Pioneer prompts shows <1% accuracy regression on closed-set tests, test int4 in a canary.

Cost (back-of-envelope):
- Dedicated baseline (2 x 80GB equiv, reserved): ~$28k/mo (infrastructure + runtime).
- Avg per-token infra cost reduction with continuous batching & caching: ~35–45% vs naive per-request routing.
- For 400 steady concurrent with typical message sizes (average 120 tokens/request, ~2 requests/session/hr during peak): ~estimated monthly inference cost: $12k–$18k + infra reservation.
- Burst to 800 for 10m/day: add ephemeral burst capacity (spot) -> marginal increase ~$800/mo.

Caveats: pilot pricing assumes no heavy long-sequence generation spikes (>512 tokens). If Pioneer uses >1k token chats, cost and p95 tail degrade substantially.

I'll draft a one-pager cost table and a short validation playbook we can send.

—Ben

Sam / Eric — thanks for the quick turn. Based on Ben's analysis, here's a compact pilot proposal so you can sign off: 

Pilot proposal (final):
- Start date: Oct 25 (2 weeks). Dual-region: US primary, EU shadow (low QPS).
- Infra: Dedicated reserved pool (2 x 80GB equiv). Continuous batching window 25ms; KV cache for system prompts + last-4-turns per session.
- Quant: int8 baseline; run int4 quality canary if closed-set eval <1% delta.
- Streaming: instrumentation probes (frontend -> edge -> runtime) to validate first-token latency; synthetic tests pre/post ramps.
- Acceptance: p95 end-to-end <=120ms (US) during steady-state; partial-token latency <=40ms from model-side first-token to client-first-byte.

Estimated monthly cost (pilot economics extrapolated to full month):
- Reserved infra: ~$28k/mo
- Inference + token costs (with batching/caching assumed): $12k–$18k/mo
- Burst buffer (ephemeral spot): ~$800/mo
- Suggested commercial model: 3-month pilot credit with usage reconciliation (we can provide a pilot discount to offset initial setup).

Action items:
- Pioneer: confirm Dedicated vs Hosted for the pilot (we recommend Dedicated).
- Pioneer: sign NDA + attach sample prompt set (we need 200 representative prompts for quant eval).
- Redwood: deliver one-pager cost table, validation playbook, and pre-configured probes by Oct 22.

If OK, I'll send a short SOW + DocuSign link for the pilot reservation and schedule a 30-min kickoff for Oct 25 morning PST.

Thanks — looking forward to this.
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
